title: Design a Ride-Sharing Service (Uber / Ola)
relevance: High — hard LLD / machine-coding staple (campus + experienced); Uber, Ola, Flipkart, Swiggy, Amazon, Microsoft, and Grab-style loops use it to probe trip state machines, Strategy for matching/pricing, Observer for status, and the driver double-assignment race.
company_notes: Campus/machine-coding staple at Flipkart, Uber, Swiggy, Ola, Amazon new-grad, and Indian product cos (~90 min working lifecycle + one match + one pricing strategy). Experienced LLD at FAANG/Uber/Grab/Microsoft goes deeper on double-assignment CAS, Strategy vs switch, Observer, TripRequest vs Trip, and geo-index interfaces. Among the top hard LLD marketplace-matching templates alongside BookMyShow, Splitwise, and food delivery.

phases.goal: Clarify functional scope, NFR concurrency/extensibility, and LLD-vs-HLD assumptions before designing classes.

must_hit.point: Mandatory FR: register riders/drivers; request ride with pickup, dropoff, and type; match available driver; accept; start; complete; cancel; compute fare.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists the full mandatory trip lifecycle FR set including register, request, match, accept, start, complete, cancel, and fare.

must_hit.point: NFR: correct under concurrent requests with no double-assign; extensible matching/pricing; modular packages; demonstrable main/CLI.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out concurrency correctness (no double-assign) plus extensible strategies and a runnable demo.

must_hit.point: State assumptions: single city / in-memory for LLD; Euclidean or Haversine OK; no pool unless asked; one active trip per driver/rider.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly scopes to in-memory single-city LLD and one active trip per driver/rider, deferring pool.

must_hit.point: Keep HLD concerns (Redis GEO, Kafka, city sharding, DISCO) as stretch — do not open the whiteboard with Kafka.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates LLD class/state/strategy/CAS focus from HLD infra and refuses to lead with Kafka.

probes: What is in scope for this LLD: on-demand only or scheduled, auto-assign vs broadcast, surge, pool, and concurrency?

hints.1: Start by listing mandatory FR for the trip lifecycle before naming classes.
hints.2: Separate mandatory FR from common extensions (surge, ratings, payment, ETA, decline/re-match) and state LLD assumptions.
hints.3: FR: register, request, match, accept, start, complete, cancel, fare; NFR: no double-assign + Strategy extensibility; assume in-memory single city; Kafka/Redis GEO only as stretch.

phases.goal: Name core domain objects, statuses, and Trip as the aggregate root with legal transitions.

must_hit.point: Core entities: Rider, Driver (+ Vehicle, DriverStatus), Trip/Ride (+ TripStatus), Location (lat/lng); optional TripRequest vs Trip, Payment, Rating.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names Rider, Driver/Vehicle/DriverStatus, Trip/TripStatus, Location, and optional TripRequest/Payment/Rating.

must_hit.point: Trip is the aggregate root: owns rider + driver refs and legal transitions; external code mutates ride state only through Trip / RideSharingService.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Treats Trip as aggregate root and forbids poking trip fields from outside the service/Trip API.

must_hit.point: TripStatus state machine: REQUESTED → DRIVER_ASSIGNED (or ACCEPTED) → IN_PROGRESS (ONGOING) → COMPLETED, with CANCELLED from pre-start states; reject illegal moves.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recites the REQUESTED/ASSIGNED/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED path plus CANCELLED from pre-start and illegal-transition rejection.

must_hit.point: DriverStatus: OFFLINE | AVAILABLE/ONLINE | ON_TRIP/IN_TRIP.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists the three driver status families used for availability and assignment.

probes: What are the core entities and who owns trip lifecycle transitions?

hints.1: List people, vehicles, trips, locations, and statuses before drawing relationships.
hints.2: Make Trip the aggregate that holds rider/driver refs and guarded status changes.
hints.3: Entities: Rider, Driver+Vehicle+DriverStatus, Trip+TripStatus, Location; Trip owns transitions REQUESTED→DRIVER_ASSIGNED→IN_PROGRESS→COMPLETED with CANCELLED pre-start.

phases.goal: Sketch the facade, strategy interfaces, catalogs, and Observer/Builder pattern surface.

must_hit.point: RideSharingService as Facade (+ optional Singleton) holding riders/drivers/trips catalogs, PricingStrategy, and DriverMatchingStrategy.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows a facade service with ConcurrentHashMap-style catalogs and injected pricing/matching strategies.

must_hit.point: PricingStrategy and DriverMatchingStrategy interfaces with concrete variants (e.g. Standard/Surge/RideType pricing; Nearest/HighestRated matching).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws strategy interfaces and at least one pricing and one matching implementation each.

must_hit.point: Patterns expected: Strategy (match+fare), State or guarded enum transitions, Observer (rider/driver status), Factory, Builder (Trip.TripBuilder), Facade; Singleton optional.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names Strategy, guarded State/enum, Observer, and Facade (plus Factory/Builder) mapped to matching, fare, lifecycle, and notify.

must_hit.point: OOD surface: MatchingStrategy.findDrivers; PricingStrategy.calculateFare; Trip.assignDriver/startTrip/endTrip/cancel; Driver.tryAssign → boolean.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the key strategy and Trip/Driver methods including tryAssign returning boolean.

probes: Walk me through the class diagram: who orchestrates, who owns algorithms, and who owns lifecycle?

hints.1: Put a single RideSharingService API in front of strategies and Trip.
hints.2: Inject MatchingStrategy and PricingStrategy; keep Trip responsible for transitions and notifications.
hints.3: Facade RideSharingService + ConcurrentHashMap catalogs; PricingStrategy/DriverMatchingStrategy; Trip state machine + Observer; Driver.tryAssign CAS hook.

phases.goal: Ship the happy-path API: register → request → accept → start → end with matching and fare.

must_hit.point: Key methods: registerRider/registerDriver, requestRide, acceptRide/declineRide, startTrip, endTrip/completeTrip, cancelTrip, updateDriverLocation, calculateFare via strategy.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Implements or sketches the full orchestration API through cancel and strategy-based fare.

must_hit.point: Matching flow: filter AVAILABLE + vehicle type (+ radius) → rank (nearest Haversine / highest rating / ETA) → atomically claim driver.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes filter-then-rank-then-claim rather than burying if-trees for assignment.

must_hit.point: Pricing: base + distance×rate + time×rate × surge (and ride-type multipliers); estimate at request, final fare at complete; surge injected, not hardcoded in Trip.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates estimate vs final fare and keeps surge as an injected multiplier via PricingStrategy.

must_hit.point: Timed path: code register → request → accept → start → end with NearestDriver + StandardFare first, then optionally add Surge.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Prioritizes a working happy path with nearest matching and standard fare before surge UML.

probes: Implement requestRide through completeTrip — how do matching and fare calculation plug in?

hints.1: Wire the mandatory path before optional product features.
hints.2: requestRide uses MatchingStrategy then claim; endTrip finalizes fare via PricingStrategy.
hints.3: register → requestRide(filter AVAILABLE+type, rank nearest, claim) → accept → start → endTrip(final fare via strategy); estimate at request, actuals at complete.

phases.goal: Show OCP via pluggable strategies and filters so surge, ratings, and ride types do not edit the facade forever.

must_hit.point: OCP: add new match/fare/ride type without editing the RideSharingService facade; strategies own algorithms, service orchestrates.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains adding Surge/HighestRated/XL via new strategy or filter classes, not switches in the facade.

must_hit.point: Add surge / premium / XL via new PricingStrategy and ride-type filter in matching — do not switch forever inside RideSharingService.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps surge/premium/XL to strategy/filter extension points.

must_hit.point: SRP/DIP: Trip owns lifecycle, strategies own algorithms, service orchestrates; depend on MatchingStrategy/PricingStrategy abstractions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Splits lifecycle vs algorithm vs orchestration and depends on strategy interfaces.

must_hit.point: Optional stretches (only if asked) stay as strategy/config hooks: pool waypoints, scheduled holds, surge by geohash zone, OTP start.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defers pool/schedule/OTP to hooks rather than reshaping the core model mid-round.

probes: How would you add surge pricing and highest-rated matching without rewriting the service?

hints.1: Avoid hardcoding nearest-driver and peak logic inside RideSharingService or Trip.
hints.2: New PricingStrategy / DriverMatchingStrategy implementations plus ride-type filters.
hints.3: setPricingStrategy/setDriverMatchingStrategy; SurgePricing and HighestRatedDriverStrategy plug in; facade stays orchestration-only.

phases.goal: Prevent double driver assignment and corrupt trip transitions under concurrent requests.

must_hit.point: Two riders must not get the same driver: prefer Driver.tryAssign / CAS (AVAILABLE → ON_TRIP) or per-driver lock — not a global lock over all matching.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows CAS or per-driver lock on availability claim and rejects city-wide synchronized matching as the senior answer.

must_hit.point: ConcurrentHashMap catalogs for riders/drivers/trips are useful but map alone ≠ atomic driver claim — still need CAS/lock per driver.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses concurrent maps for catalogs while insisting claim is a separate atomic operation.

must_hit.point: Synchronize Trip transitions so cancel vs start cannot corrupt state — lock the Trip (or optimistic version), not the whole service.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Scopes locking to the Trip for cancel-vs-start races rather than locking the facade.

must_hit.point: On CAS fail, retry next candidate; loser of the double-assign race re-matches.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes failed claim → next candidate / re-match rather than leaving a stuck assignment.

probes: Two riders request; both see the same nearest AVAILABLE driver — how do you prevent double assignment?

hints.1: Read-then-write on driver status is the race — claim must be atomic.
hints.2: Use Driver.tryAssign / CAS AVAILABLE→ON_TRIP or a per-driver lock; ConcurrentHashMap alone is not enough.
hints.3: Filter candidates, then tryAssign; on false, pick next driver; Trip cancel/start synchronized on the Trip object, not a global service lock.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Auto-assign is simpler for a 90 min round; broadcast matches real Uber UX but needs offer TTL plus an accept race — state both and implement one.
Hardcoded matching/pricing can pass a demo, but Strategy is the expected answer when asked to add surge, highest-rated, or XL-only without editing the facade.

tradeoffs.topic: Enum-guarded transitions vs full State pattern classes
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Enum + IllegalStateException is the interview default; full State classes win only if many behaviors diverge per status — avoid over-engineering mid-round.
A coarse global lock is correct but serializes the city; per-driver CAS or lock shows senior handling of the double-assignment race.

gotchas.trap: Two riders, one nearest driver — race on read-then-write availability.
gotchas.correction: Show tryAssign / CAS / UPDATE … WHERE status=AVAILABLE; the loser re-matches.

gotchas.trap: Driver declines or no accept within TTL leaves Trip stuck in REQUESTED.
gotchas.correction: Offer the next candidate or fail with no drivers; do not leave the trip REQUESTED forever.

gotchas.trap: Adding surge / premium / XL by growing switches inside RideSharingService.
gotchas.correction: Add a new PricingStrategy and ride-type filter in matching instead of endless switch in the facade.

gotchas.trap: Cancel after driver arrived / mid-trip without a product rule.
gotchas.correction: Cancel from ASSIGNED is a legal transition (fee is product); cancel from IN_PROGRESS is illegal unless specified.

gotchas.trap: Pool / shared rides assumed in scope without asking.
gotchas.correction: Say out of scope early unless insisted — multiple waypoints/riders reshape the model.

gotchas.trap: Fare math living inside Driver or treating estimate as final charge.
gotchas.correction: Put fare in PricingStrategy/FareCalculator; estimate at request ≠ final charge at complete.

gotchas.trap: Opening an LLD round with Redis/Kafka.
gotchas.correction: Interviewers want classes, Trip state machine, strategies, and CAS — not HLD.

gotchas.trap: Singleton god-service that prices, matches, pays, and notifies inline.
gotchas.correction: Split MatchingStrategy/PricingStrategy plus Observer (or callbacks) or design score drops.

gotchas.trap: Finishing surge UML without a working request → accept → complete path.
gotchas.correction: Ship the mandatory happy path first, then add Surge strategy.
